definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 (4.34) defines class of a data item by 'the PICTURE clause, the USAGE clause, or the PICTURE and USAGE clauses'; §2023:3.33 says 'the specific clauses' and moves PICTURE/USAGE to a note. The operative table, §2002:8.5.2 Table 3, is §2023:8.5.2.1 Table 2 less the 2023-only class message-tag and category function-pointer, with the same group-item rules, so 'a data item of any class or category' is every 2002 class of Table 3 plus strongly-typed groups (class = type-name, §2002:8.5.2). The reader's probes p4/p5/p6 at 2002 cover them. Scope unchanged.

pending-clause.answer: Invoked by 'type-name' and clause 15. §2002:8.5.3 types: 'A type is a template that contains all the characteristics of a data item', the same TYPEDEF types AR1 admits; §2002:8.5.4 zero-length items (ODO-zero groups, ANY LENGTH) are data items AR1 admits, their length is the returned-value rule's; §2002:14.5.8 is MOVE alignment, unrelated; 8.8.1.x has no role (no arithmetic). §2002:15 and §2002:15.1 differ from 2023 15.1/15.2 only in the function-type text (2002 15.1 says 'The number of character positions in this data item is specified in the function definition'; 2023 adds the sentence on type determining use); both describe the returned item. Argument classes are in §2002:15.2, whose argument types the reader cited; this argument rule does not rest on the changed text.
